messages.subject: RE: [TMB users] Use of exp, log, etc with arrays and matrices
messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] Use of exp, log, etc with arrays and matrices
messages.body_plain:
TMB arrays are not Eigen arrays (see the array documentation):

- The TMB array class extends the eigen array with arbitrary dimension.
- Side-effect: You can't expect all TMB array methods to work as in R.

In your example:

DATA_ARRAY(a1);
array<Type> a1_exp = exp(a1);

The exp operator is not explicitly implemented for the TMB array. When applying exp to a1 the array is 'downgraded' to an Eigen array, i.e. the dimension attribute is lost. Fortunately, you get the error already at compile time. The workaround is to expand the code like this:

array<Type> a1_exp(a1.dim);
a1_exp = exp(a1);

From: tmb-...@googlegroups.com [tmb-...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of betasci007 [betas...@gmail.com]
Sent: Wednesday, November 30, 2016 11:56 PM
To: TMB Users
Subject: [TMB users] Use of exp, log, etc with arrays and matrices

Hi Group

I have been exploring the Eigen capabilities within TMB and have been able to get many of the functions to work. I am a bit stumped on the use of exp though. I have matrices and arrays for which I want to apply exp to each cell.

As seen from the attached files, exp will work on matrices converted to arrays but does not seem to work on matrices or arrays directly. I tried all sorts of combos of array() and matrix() with exp, all to not avail. I see in the TMB documentation a matexp function but have not been able to get this to work.

Any ideas?

Bob

--

messages.subject: Using romberg approximation in MakeADFun?
messages.body_plain:
Dear TMB developers,

Thanks for this great TMB package. I learn that TMB uses Laplace approximation by default, but it may be not appropriate for categorical data (e.g.,
Accuracy of Laplace approximation for discrete response mixed models; http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167947308002533). Can I use other approximation such as romberg in MakeADFun?

Best,

CW

messages.subject: Re: Using romberg approximation in MakeADFun?
messages.body_plain:
Alternatives to the Laplace approximation are not yet available via MakeADFun.

You can use other methods but it will require more work.
Fore example, here is how to use adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature from within the template:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_examples/adaptive_integration.cpp

A (partial) example of Romberg integration is also available:

http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/namespaceromberg.html

Something like this would apply for categorical data as well. It might be useful to add a Romberg-version of 'tmb_examples/socatt.cpp' ?

messages.subject: Rows vs columns
messages.body_plain:
Hi TMBers

I have been experimenting with TMB, exploring various data extractions and manipulations, using a simple state space model I obtained at the Nov 2015 ICES course. In ADMB, I have been using time as rows and whatever variable as columns and wanted to do the same in TMB. In the TMB state space model, in the estimation of the likelihoods, when I tried to extract the u and obs variables by row using x.row(i), the program bombed. I had to transpose the u and obs arrays and then extract the data using x.col(i). All the relevant files are attached. In the wiki archive, a previous message by Kasper states that row extraction is expensive but I was surprised that it didn't work at all.

Comments?

Bob

messages.subject: Re: Rows vs columns
messages.body_plain:
You could use matrices instead of arrays:

* Replace "_ARRAY" by "_MATRIX".
* Replace "obs.dim(0)" by "obs.rows()".
* Replace "obs.dim(1)" by "obs.cols()".

That should work.
